html:
The Puyallup are a Coast Salish people of the Puyallup River and Commencement Bay, where the city of Tacoma, Washington, now stands. They speak Lushootseed.

They fished for salmon in the river and bay, gathered shellfish and traded by canoe across southern Puget Sound with the Nisqually, Muckleshoot and Steilacoom. Under the Treaty of Medicine Creek of 1854 they gave up most of their land but kept the right to fish at their usual places.

When Washington State arrested Native fishers in the 1960s, the Puyallup were at the centre of the Fish Wars. The Boldt decision of 1974 upheld treaty fishing rights. In the late 1980s the tribe settled its land claims with the United States. See also Coast Salish.
